Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Conversation, family & daily routines

favourite adjective and noun

also favorite, my favourite, best-loved, the favourite

classical

Plin. Ep. 1.3.1: Cōmum, tuae meaeque dēliciae
Cic. Att. 1.5.8: Tulliola dēliciae nostrae

dēliciae, dēliciārum f. pl.

noun, first declension, plural

one’s favourite, darling, delight (a person, a place, a thing)

To be someone’s favourite is in dēliciīs esse alicui (Lewis & Short). Titus was amor ac dēliciae generis hūmānī (Suet. Tit. 1, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • maximē placet — is my favourite, I like it best

    phrase: placeō with the dative · classical · Cic. Att. 2.4.1: mihi maximē placet

    Latin has no adjective for “favourite”; it says what pleases most, as in the household question Quid tibi maximē placuit? (see what did you like best?).

  • cārissimus, cārissima, cārissimum — dearest

    adjective (superlative of cārus) · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.14.2: meae cārissimae animae

Examples

  • quid agit Cōmum, tuae meaeque dēliciae?

    how is Comum, your favourite place and mine?Plin. Ep. 1.3.1

  • Tulliola dēliciae nostrae

    little Tullia, our darlingCic. Att. 1.5.8

  • Quī color tibi maximē placet?

    What’s your favourite colour?composed

See also darling, what did you like best?, love, colour.
